answer: The quill test I would run is Chartered radio presenter record with radio academy attestation: shows the academy recorded across years of stations, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that shows the academy recorded across years of stations — so privacy survives, and the vault is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. A farm could afford one proof, maybe ten, but the oasis of a hundred is measured in weeks of work and thousands in fees, against a reward that shrinks per head.
